q: For what purpose did Yahweh send an ambassador among the nations?
a: Yahweh sent an ambassador among the nations to cause the nations to rise up for battle against Edom.

q: What was one of the sins of the Edomites?
a: The Edomites had pride in their hearts and believed that they could not be brought down to the ground.

q: Who will deceive and prevail against Edom?
a: The men who had an alliance of peace with Edom will deceive and prevail against Edom.

q: Why will Edom be covered with shame and cut off forever?
a: Edom will be covered with shame and cut off forever because of the violence Edom did to his brother Jacob.

q: What happened on the day that Edom stood aloof from Jacob?
a: On that day, strangers entered the gates of Jacob and took captive its wealth.

q: What did Yahweh tell Edom not to do regarding Judah in the day of Judah’s distress?
a: Yahweh said that Edom should not have looked, rejoiced, or made their mouth great.

q: What did Yahweh tell Edom not to do regarding Judah in the day of Judah’s calamity?
a: Yahweh said that Edom should not have entered Judah’s gates, rejoiced, or looted Judah’s wealth in the day of Judah’s calamity.

q: What did Yahweh say would return on Edom’s head?
a: Yahweh said that Edom’s recompense would return on Edom’s head.

q: What would some in Mount Zion be able to do despite the distress of Judah?
a: Some in Mount Zion would be able to escape despite the distress of Judah.

q: How many of Edom would escape the judgment of Yahweh?
a: There would be no survivors in Edom after Yahweh’s judgment.

q: Who would then possess the mount of Esau?
a: Those from the Negev would then possess the mount of Esau.

q: From where would the mountain of Esau then be judged?
a: The mountain of Esau would then be judged from Mount Zion.
